# Model completeness

<!-- Generated by scripts/completeness/report.py; do not edit by hand. -->

Whether the model of each CCNL is complete, so that only the comparison
with real payslips is left. A CCNL is complete when its census lists its
requirements and nothing the model owes it is open: no open requirement,
no weak payable rule (`assumed` or `missing`) it reads, no open limitation
with a monetary impact, none whose fact has no input (`outside_input`),
and no capability left to the caller, partial or not computed.
A CCNL whose only remaining limitations are declared residuals
(`unsourced`: a documented search of the law, the INPS and Ministry
practice and the signed text found no source and no statutory default)
is *complete except declared residuals*: no open work is left, but the
runs those residuals concern stay not payable, so it is not complete.
Completeness is not readiness and not external validation: readiness is
shown for reference only, and
[the validation matrix](validation-matrix.md) tracks the comparisons.
`scripts/completeness/report.py --strict` fails while any CCNL is
incomplete.

**Complete: 3/136 CCNLs**; complete except declared residuals: 0. Bundle: 251 weak rules, 284 open limitations (284 with a monetary impact), 31 declared residuals.

## Declared window

Every CCNL is assessed from 2026-01-01 to 2027-12-31, the supported tax years. Pay tables that start after the first day or end before the last are a gap of the CCNL. The history the engine reads from before the window (the INPS sickness base of the month before, the progressive amounts of the year) comes from the opening state and the prior-year facts of the request, not from the bundle.

Future data, registered apart from the gaps: a contract whose validity ends inside the window keeps its last tables until the renewal (column *Renewal due*), and these resources carry the values of the year before because their sources are not published yet (their weak rules and the engine limitations `parental_income_condition`, `provisional_inps_ruleset`, `provisional_ruleset` are not counted as gaps):

- `contribution/2027/agricoltura.json`
- `contribution/2027/artigianato.json`
- `contribution/2027/credito.json`
- `contribution/2027/edilizia.json`
- `contribution/2027/industria.json`
- `contribution/2027/lavoro-domestico.json`
- `contribution/2027/pubblica-amministrazione.json`
- `contribution/2027/terziario.json`
- `family/2027.json`
- `irpef/work_deduction/2027.json`
- `sector/2027/agricoltura.json`
- `sector/2027/artigianato.json`
- `sector/2027/credito.json`
- `sector/2027/edilizia.json`
- `sector/2027/industria.json`
- `sector/2027/lavoro-domestico.json`
- `sector/2027/pubblica-amministrazione.json`
- `sector/2027/terziario.json`
- `surtax/municipal/2027.json`
- `surtax/regional/2027.json`
- `tax_credit/somma_esente/2027.json`
- `variable_pay/2027.json`

Capabilities a caller value may replace are not counted as gaps when the engine computes them from a rule the CCNL holds (`absence`, `holiday_work`, `night_work`, `overtime`, `shift_work`, `travel_allowance`), nor when their amount is a fact only the employer knows:

- `bilateral_funds`: the funds the CCNL sets are computed by contractual_funds; the event carries a territorial or company fund the bundle does not hold
- `company_supplement`: the elements of a company agreement are a fact of the employer (EmployerProfile.second_level_elements)
- `contract_renewal_arrears`: the arrears are the difference from what earlier payslips paid, a fact of the employer's payroll; the una tantum the CCNL sets is computed by una_tantum
- `territorial_supplement`: the elements of a territorial agreement are a fact of the employer (EmployerProfile.second_level_elements)
